note: Per bench, runtime and scenario: v1 cost over its raw twin's, the median of 3 interleaved pass medians, from the RATIO lines of the hot-path benchmark job of every CI run below, judged and record alike (bench/src/derive-ceilings.ts). A bench pools the runs whose bench/src/<bench>.ts and bench/src/gate.ts match the newest run's. Ceiling (packages/core/tests/e2e/ceiling-rule.ts): per scenario, fit log(ratio) (mean m, sample sd s), sigma_upper = s * sqrt((n-1)/chi2_0.10,n-1), z = Phi^-1(1 - 0.02/G) with G the gated scenarios, ceiling = max(worst x 1.35, exp(m + z*sigma_upper)); baseline the median; catches = ceiling / baseline. A ratio cancels runner speed, not CPU microarchitecture, so a scenario whose level differs by model carries a reason naming its per-model levels and its catch on the lowest. A same-runner A/B gate (head vs a pinned base commit) replaces these ceilings next. A reportOnly scenario is printed and never fails the run. No retry: a red with v1 unchanged is answered by a re-derive over more runs, never a rerun until green.
